lessons.title: An t- roimh ghuta: ainmfhocal firinscneach
lessons.en: Masculine nouns: t- before a vowel
lessons.rule: Irish has no word for a: árasán means flat or a flat. The only article is an (the). A masculine noun that begins with a consonant does not change after an (an bus, an doras), but a masculine noun that begins with a vowel takes t- joined to it with a hyphen: an t-árasán, an t-uisce. Before a capital letter there is no hyphen: an tIúr.
steps: Is the noun masculine? árasán is (it ends in -án).
Does it begin with a vowel? Yes, á.
Put t- in front of it: an t-árasán.

example.prompt: Tá an (árasán) i lár an Iúir.
example.answer: Tá an t-árasán i lár an Iúir.

more.answer: Chonaic mé an t-éan sa ghairdín.

lessons.hint: Masculine + vowel: an t-. Masculine + consonant: no change.

items.prompt: Tá an (uisce) i Loch nEathach fuar.
items.answer: Tá an t-uisce i Loch nEathach fuar.
Ghlan mé an t-urlár sa chistin.
Cá bhfuil an t-ospidéal is gaire?
Tháinig an t-eitleán isteach go déanach.
Scríobh an t-ainm ar an chóipleabhar.
D'ith sé an t-úll sa charr.
Bhí an t-aisteoir iontach sa scannán.

lessons.title: Ainmfhocal baininscneach: an + séimhiú
lessons.rule: After an, a feminine noun that begins with b, c, f, g, m or p takes séimhiú: bean becomes an bhean, fuinneog becomes an fhuinneog. Nouns that begin with d or t never take séimhiú after an, whatever their gender: an deirfiúr, an teilifís. A feminine noun that begins with a vowel does not change: an oíche.
steps: Is the noun feminine? fuinneog is (it ends in -eog).
Does it begin with b, c, f, g, m or p? Yes, f.
Add h after the first letter: an fhuinneog.

example.answer: Druid an fhuinneog, le do thoil.

more.answer: Tá an bhean ag an doras.

more.prompt: Tá an (deirfiúr) s'agam ina cónaí i mBéal Feirste.
more.answer: Tá an deirfiúr s'agam ina cónaí i mBéal Feirste.

lessons.hint: Feminine: an + h. But d, t and vowels stay as they are.

items.answer: Tá an ghirseach sin i mo rang.

items.answer: D'oscail sí an oifig ar a naoi.

lessons.title: An ts: ainmfhocal baininscneach le s
lessons.en: Feminine nouns beginning with s: an ts
lessons.rule: A feminine noun that begins with s followed by a vowel, or by l, n or r, takes t in front after an, with no hyphen: sráid becomes an tsráid, slí becomes an tslí. A masculine noun beginning with s does not change (an siopa, an samhradh), and sc, sm, sp and st never change (an scoil, an spéir).
steps: Is the noun feminine? sráid is.
Is the s followed by a vowel, l, n or r? Yes, r.
Put t in front of it: an tsráid.
lessons.hint: Feminine s + vowel, l, n or r: an ts. Masculine s, or sc, sm, sp, st: no change.

items.answer: Bhí an tseachtain seo caite fada.

items.answer: Tá an sneachta bán ar Shliabh gCuillinn.

lessons.title: Na + h roimh ghuta
lessons.en: Plural: na, and h before a vowel
lessons.rule: In the plural the article is na for every noun, masculine or feminine. Na leaves a consonant as it is, so the séimhiú of the singular goes (an bhróg, na bróga). Before a vowel na puts h, and the t- of the singular goes: an t-úll becomes na húlla.
steps: Use the plural: éan becomes éin.
It begins with a vowel, so put h in front: na héin.

example.prompt: Iolra: Tá an t-éan sa chrann. (éin)

more.prompt: Iolra: Tá an cailín ag canadh. (cailíní)

lessons.hint: Plural: na. Vowel: na h-. The t- and the séimhiú go.

lessons.title: Firinscneach nó baininscneach? Na deirí
lessons.rule: Some endings tell you the gender. Feminine: -óg and -eog (fuinneog), -lann (bialann), and -acht or -íocht in a word of more than one syllable (Gaeltacht, filíocht). Masculine: -ín (cailín), -án (cupán), -óir, -eoir and -éir (múinteoir, úinéir), -aire (iascaire) and -adh (geimhreadh). Once you know the gender, you know what an does: an bhialann, an cupán, an t-úinéir.
steps: Look at the ending: bialann ends in -lann.
Feminine with b: add h after an, so an bhialann.

example.answer: Tá an bhialann ar an phríomhshráid.

lessons.title: An t-alt: cleachtadh measctha
lessons.rule: Put it all together. The prompt tells you the gender (fir. is firinscneach, masculine; bain. is baininscneach, feminine). Masculine: t- before a vowel, no change to a consonant. Feminine: séimhiú on b, c, f, g, m, p; t before s + vowel, l, n or r; no change to d, t, sc, sm, sp, st or a vowel.
steps: Read the gender in the brackets: bain.
Check the first letter: b takes séimhiú.

example.prompt: Chonaic mé an (bó: bain.) sa pháirc.
example.answer: Chonaic mé an bhó sa pháirc.

more.prompt: Tá an (athair: fir.) ag obair san Iúr.
more.answer: Tá an t-athair ag obair san Iúr.

lessons.hint: fir.: t- before a vowel. bain.: h, or ts before s.
